title: Human-in-the-loop
summary: Human-in-the-loop systems pause execution where a person must supply judgment or authorization.
overview: A durable checkpoint preserves the proposed action while the system waits. Resumption must account for changed state and any code that the runtime executes again.
why: An approval is useful only when the reviewer can understand the action being approved.
example: Before applying a database migration, show the exact migration and target environment, persist the decision, and recheck prerequisites on resume.
judgment: Choose approval boundaries and invalidate approval when the proposed action materially changes.
next: What happens if the target schema changes while a migration awaits review?
